statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 20% at the bottom of the watch band as about 71% of the overnight Micron-led advance is retraced on expanding turnover, while firmer oil and a higher long end keep Stress at 75%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold and steps down two points to 20%. The preceding assessment named rejection beneath 31,094.75 as the condition for a step back into the watch band; that condition has now extended into a deep retracement, with roughly 319 of the 449-point overnight advance given back over two hours on rising turnover and price returned to the 30,812.75 shelf. No amplifier remains observed: acceptance above the pivot is gone, price does not hold the session extreme, and the extension sequence has ended in a measurable two-way test. Mapped policy state is WATCH. The 12:00-15:00Z danger window covering jobless claims, Fed's Barkin, the cash open, the final manufacturing PMI and ISM manufacturing remains the hour range where observed post-release continuation would warrant renewed escalation.
headline: NQ fades 319 points from 31,147.75 back to the 30,812.75 shelf on expanding turnover, easing Tail to 20% while WTI clears 92 dollars and Brent touches 100
body: December E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures trade 30,829.00, up 130.25 points or 0.42% from the 30,698.75 settle, after retracing roughly 319 points from the overnight high at 31,147.75. A second corroborating source prints 30,822.00, up 0.40%, on about 108,845 contracts. The decisive development this hour is the depth and quality of the fade: the overnight advance measured 449 points and about 71% of it has now been given back, taking price roughly 265 points below the 31,094.75 pivot that earlier assessments identified as the marker of genuine uptrend resumption and returning it to the 30,812.75 shelf. Turnover has expanded again to 109.17k from 84.66k an hour earlier, so the retracement has developed on improving rather than deteriorating liquidity across two consecutive hours. That is the signature of a functioning two-way market, and it is the direct opposite of the pathological no-retracement path the Tail score measures. The advance had an identifiable driver in Micron's fiscal fourth quarter, which reported 54.23 billion dollars of revenue, GAAP diluted earnings of 32.87 dollars per share and an 86.8% gross margin, with first-quarter revenue guided to 61.5 billion dollars plus or minus 1.5 billion and gross margin to roughly 86%, alongside a caution that margins would narrow; that result lifted Japan's Nikkei 225 by 2.8% and the Kospi by 1.2%, and the index-futures fade since then has not been accompanied by any new negative company-level catalyst. Cross-assets continue to conflict with the equity path rather than confirm it, and the conflict has intensified. WTI has extended to 92.40 dollars, up 2.19%, and Brent to 100.04 dollars, up 2.05%, with Middle East flows recovering toward pre-war levels at 13.2 million barrels per day through the Strait of Hormuz and half of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline capacity restored, set against an unresolved US-Iran impasse. The 2-year sits at 4.92%, the 5-year 5.13%, the 10-year 5.33% and the 30-year 5.68%, every tenor higher on the day, with the 10-year and 30-year at their highest since 2002 on energy-driven inflation and fiscal concern. The VIX is 16.72, up 2.33% from 16.34. The completed 30 September cash session continues to argue that reversion is intact: the Dow fell 0.86% and the S&P 500 0.25% while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.23% and NDX closed 30,408.50, up 0.23%, at the exact low of a 30,408.50 to 30,630.45 range and therefore a complete intraday fade. August core PCE at 0.2% monthly and 3.0% annually against 3.3% expected has cut October Fed hike odds to roughly 35% from about 50%. Firmer oil and a higher long end against fading equities is a risk-negative mix, but under the standing contract it raises Stress rather than Tail while the equity price path itself is mean-reverting. Stress therefore firms to 75% and Tail eases two further points to 20%, the bottom of the watch band, mapping the policy state to WATCH. Shared Finviz context was collected 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with partial collection status, so at roughly 33 hours old it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used; this assessment rests entirely on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail sat at 15-16% through the European and early US hours of 30 September with the mode mixed, stepped into the watch band at 20% from 12:00Z as the US data block and the long-end selloff developed, and peaked at 23% around 15:00-16:00Z. It held a 20-22% range through the US afternoon and the early Asian session, then firmed steadily from 20% at 00:00Z through 21%, 22% and 23% to 24% at 05:00Z and 25% at 06:00Z as NQ printed successive fresh overnight highs and accepted above its named 31,094.75 pivot, with the mode turning trend-up in those two slots. The 07:00Z slot returned to 22% and the mixed mode once the first liquid two-way test produced a measurable 188-point retracement. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 65% and 74%, and Confidence held 85-88%.
outlookSummary: The mapped danger window is unchanged at 12:00-15:00Z, covering initial and continuing jobless claims at 12:30Z against a consensus near 200K after 197K, Fed's Barkin at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z with ISM consensus a touch above the 54.6 prior. Forecast Tail opens at 20% at the bottom of the watch band and holds there across the mid-European hours where the fullest two-way book of the pre-US session normally extends a retracement, firms to 21-22% into the claims hour, and peaks at the top of the watch band at 24% across the 14:00Z ISM hour where Stress tops at 79%. It decays to 20-22% through the US afternoon, the 20:00Z cash close and the late evening, then firms to 21-23% through the Asian session and the European pre-open as positioning concentrates ahead of the September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October, which falls outside this forecast window. The forecast peak deliberately stops at the top of the watch band rather than crossing into the block band, because a scheduled event stack is a checkpoint and the observed path has supplied no amplifiers. A renewed upward reassessment would require observed evidence rather than schedule: shallow or failed retracements after the cash open, repeated extension following a failed pullback, a reclaim of 31,094.75 and the 31,147.75 high without an intervening retracement, or the long end finally realigning behind the equity move. A break of the 30,812.75 shelf that extends without a pause would be the downside equivalent, while containment inside the 30,812.75 to 31,094.75 band through the US session would support a further step down within the watch band.
